fields.Participants: Dept Supervisor, LP Officer, Store Manager, Receiving Clerk
fields.Trigger: Staff identifies suspected counterfeit during receiving, stocking, or customer interaction

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "printing, color, material" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-scan of "Supervisor conducts initial assessment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates confirmed cases to LP Manager for full investigation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **False positives**: Genuine products with manufacturing variations flagged incorrectly
- **Evidence contamination**: Staff handling may compromise forensic evidence
System Touchpoints: - LP case management system with photo evidence upload
- Product authentication scan via mobile app
- Inventory quarantine with LP hold status

steps.activity: Staff member identifies suspected counterfeit: packaging quality deviation (printing, color, material), product weight/feel difference, missing security features (hologram, serialization QR), price discrepancy with market; escalates to Department Supervisor

Supervisor conducts initial assessment: compares against authentic reference sample, scans QR code (if present), checks serial number in system; if suspected counterfeit confirmed: segregates product in LP quarantine area, documents with photos, logs in LP case system

LP Officer conducts on-site investigation within 48 hours: collects evidence (product, packaging, labels), traces product origin (PO → GR → shelf), determines if breach occurred at vendor, DC, or store level; escalates confirmed cases to LP Manager for full investigation (W2559)

fields.Participants: LP Manager, LP Officer, Legal, Procurement, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Confirmed counterfeit detection requiring full investigation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-assign of "assigns case number, assigns LP Officer as lead investigator" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews CCTV footage of receiving and stocking areas" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "counterfeit, supply chain diversion, internal substitution" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-443 (ensure controlled execution — Counterfeit Detection & Investigation (PA-71.2).)
- operational: LP Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Investigation delays**: Staff interviews and CCTV review are time-consuming
- **Legal exposure**: Incorrect accusation of vendor or staff creates liability
System Touchpoints: - LP case management with investigation workflow
- Supply chain traceability (PO → GR → shelf tracking)
- CCTV review system with transaction timestamp correlation

steps.activity: LP Manager initiates formal investigation: assigns case number, assigns LP Officer as lead investigator; determines scope (single product, vendor, store, category); sets investigation timeline (target: 30-day resolution)

LP Officer collects evidence: product samples, packaging, labeling; traces supply chain (vendor PO → shipment → GR → putaway → shelf); interviews relevant staff (receiving clerk, stock associate, department supervisor); reviews CCTV footage of receiving and stocking areas

LP Officer compiles investigation report: root cause determination (vendor-supplied counterfeit, supply chain diversion, internal substitution), evidence chain of custody, financial impact assessment; LP Manager reviews and determines action: vendor notification, contract action, staff discipline, law enforcement referral

fields.Participants: LP Manager, Procurement, Legal, Vendor Brand Protection
fields.Trigger: Confirmed counterfeit product traced to vendor supply

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "counterfeit sample details, batch/lot information, quantity affected,…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-measure of "Vendor confirms authenticity status" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "update vendor contract" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-443 (ensure controlled execution — Counterfeit Detection & Investigation (PA-71.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor denial**: Vendors may resist acknowledging counterfeit supply
- **Supply disruption**: Suspending vendor orders during investigation affects product availability
System Touchpoints: - LP case management with vendor notification workflow
- Vendor scorecard with counterfeit incident flagging
- Contract management system with anti-counterfeit clauses

steps.activity: LP Manager notifies vendor brand protection team: provides counterfeit sample details, batch/lot information, quantity affected, photographic evidence; requests vendor authentication assessment and batch trace

Vendor confirms authenticity status; if confirmed counterfeit from vendor supply: Procurement suspends pending orders from affected batch, arranges product return/replacement, negotiates vendor responsibility (replacement, credit, investigation cost contribution); if vendor supply chain compromised: vendor implements corrective measures

LP Manager and Legal update vendor contract: add anti-counterfeit clause with penalties, require vendor serialization and authentication cooperation, establish joint investigation protocol; includes vendor scorecard impact for counterfeit incidents

fields.Participants: VP Legal, LP Manager, NBI/DTI, Law Enforcement
fields.Trigger: Large-scale counterfeiting case or organized counterfeiting ring identified

workflows.name: Law Enforcement & Regulatory Reporting for Counterfeiting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepares formal complaint" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "counterfeiting, DTI for consumer protection violations, local PNP for criminal…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks case progress" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Prosecution difficulty**: Philippine IP enforcement is slow and resource-intensive
- **Retaliation risk**: Organized counterfeiters may retaliate against stores or staff; mitigated by standard operating procedures and system-enforced validation rules
System Touchpoints: - LP case management with law enforcement referral tracking
- Document management for legal filings
- Evidence chain of custody tracking

steps.activity: VP Legal evaluates case for law enforcement referral: severity (value, volume, organized ring indicator), strength of evidence, jurisdictional considerations; for qualifying cases (typically >PHP 200K value or organized operation): prepares formal complaint

Legal files complaint with appropriate agency: NBI Intellectual Property Rights Division for organized counterfeiting, DTI for consumer protection violations, local PNP for criminal cases; provides evidence package, sworn statements, product samples

Legal coordinates with law enforcement: provides testimony, expert witnesses, additional evidence as requested; tracks case progress; protects BuildRight interests and reputation throughout proceedings

fields.Participants: Customer Service Mgr, LP Officer, Store Manager, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer returns product confirmed or suspected as counterfeit

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "checks product against authentication database" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "logs in evidence system" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "LP Officer uses case for investigation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fraud risk**: Customer may present counterfeit not purchased from BuildRight; mitigated by CTL-233 (anti-counterfeit program integrity)
- **Brand reputation**: Counterfeit incidents at BuildRight damage customer trust
System Touchpoints: - Customer return with counterfeit flag
- LP evidence collection with product seizure
- Purchase history validation

steps.activity: Customer reports suspected counterfeit: presents product and receipt; Customer Service verifies purchase history, checks product against authentication database; if confirmed or highly suspected counterfeit: immediately offers resolution

Resolution options: (a) Full refund + replacement with genuine product, (b) Store credit with 10% goodwill bonus, (c) Upgrade to higher-spec genuine product at no additional cost; LP Officer collects suspected counterfeit and logs in evidence system

LP Officer uses case for investigation: traces product source, determines if from BuildRight stock (internal issue) or customer-acquired elsewhere and falsely claiming; for confirmed BuildRight-sourced counterfeits: escalates to full investigation (W2559)

fields.Participants: LP Analyst, LP Manager, Legal, Marketplace Platforms
fields.Trigger: Weekly monitoring scan or vendor brand alert

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitors online marketplaces" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "checks if seller is authorized dealer" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Legal follows up on takedown requests" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Whack-a-mole**: Counterfeit sellers relist under new accounts after takedown
- **Platform cooperation**: Some platforms slow to act on takedown requests
System Touchpoints: - Online marketplace monitoring tools
- Brand registry portals (Shopee Brand Protection, Lazada IP Protection)
- Takedown request tracking

steps.activity: LP Analyst monitors online marketplaces (Shopee, Lazada, FB Marketplace, Carousell): searches for BuildRight-exclusive brands, private label products, high-risk categories (power tools, electrical); identifies suspicious listings based on pricing (significantly below SRP), product imagery (BuildRight packaging used without authorization), seller location patterns

Analyst validates suspicious listings: purchases sample for authentication (if warranted), cross-references with BuildRight serial numbers, checks if seller is authorized dealer; for confirmed counterfeits: files takedown request with marketplace platform using brand registry tools

Legal follows up on takedown requests: tracks platform response timeline (typically 3–7 days), escalates non-responsive platforms, coordinates with vendor brand protection teams for joint takedown actions; maintains marketplace enforcement log

fields.Participants: LP Analyst, LP Manager, Category Manager

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scan, visual, customer report" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Analyst performs threat assessment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "LP Manager presents findings to Category Manager and COO" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-443 (ensure controlled execution — Counterfeit Detection & Investigation (PA-71.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Underreporting**: Many counterfeits go undetected; actual counterfeit rate likely higher than reported
- **Resource constraint**: LP team of 20 officers across 200 stores limits investigation capacity
System Touchpoints: - LP analytics dashboard with counterfeit incident tracking
- Trend analysis and heat map visualization
- Category risk scoring

steps.activity: LP Analyst compiles counterfeit trend data: incidents by category (power tools highest risk), by brand, by source (vendor, DC, store, external), by geographic region, by detection method (QR scan, visual, customer report); calculates counterfeit rate per 10,000 units sold

Analyst performs threat assessment: identifies emerging counterfeiting patterns (new categories, improved fake quality), seasonal trends (holiday season spike), high-risk vendors or stores; produces risk heat map by category and region

LP Manager presents findings to Category Manager and COO: recommends prevention investments (additional serialization categories, enhanced inspection procedures), enforcement priorities (focus on highest-loss categories), vendor engagement actions; updates annual anti-counterfeit strategy

fields.Participants: LP Manager, HR, Store Managers, Ethics Committee
fields.Trigger: Annual program cycle or internal counterfeit incident

workflows.name: Internal Counterfeit Prevention & Staff Integrity Program

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "LP Manager designs internal prevention program" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "counterfeit awareness, ethical sourcing obligations, consequence framework for…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "checks at stores, receiving area CCTV monitoring, serial number reconciliation…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-443 (ensure controlled execution — Counterfeit Detection & Investigation (PA-71.2).)
- operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Internal collusion**: Staff facilitating counterfeit introduction or product diversion
- **Culture resistance**: Anti-counterfeit measures perceived as distrust of employees
System Touchpoints: - LMS with integrity certification tracking
- Anonymous tip reporting system
- LP spot-check scheduling and documentation

steps.activity: LP Manager designs internal prevention program: staff integrity expectations regarding product authentication, prohibited activities (selling personal items on store floor, facilitating gray market diversion), whistleblower protection, anonymous reporting hotline

HR delivers integrity training: included in new hire orientation and annual refresher; covers counterfeit awareness, ethical sourcing obligations, consequence framework for facilitating counterfeiting or diversion; sign annual integrity pledge

LP Manager implements preventive controls: surprise authentication spot-checks at stores, receiving area CCTV monitoring, serial number reconciliation for high-risk categories, tip investigation within 48 hours; maintains confidential reporting channel
